title: Anesthesia Acupuncture Advanced Clinical Experience
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Accreditation: Not ACGME-accredited; Advanced Clinical Experience (ACE) — participants are appointed as Instructors and the position is not classified as a fellowship or postdoctoral training appointment
Summary: A one-year advanced experience providing clinical and research experience in medical acupuncture, with the option to specialise in adult or pediatric acupuncture, completion of medical acupuncture certification and clinical research training.

title: Advanced Training in Medical Education
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Early or mid-career physicians seeking a career in medical education
Accreditation: Not ACGME-accredited; Advanced Clinical Experience (ACE) — participants are appointed as Instructors and the position is not classified as a fellowship or postdoctoral training appointment
Summary: An advanced training opportunity for early or mid-career physicians to develop as medical education leaders through a keystone medical education project, 12 hours per week of clinical work in the Stanford operating rooms, and access to Stanford teaching and simulation programmes.

title: Advanced Clinical Experience in Liver Transplant Anesthesiology
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Start: July or August (flexible case by case)
Deadline: Rolling; applications accepted starting one year prior to projected start date
Eligibility: Completed residency training in Anesthesiology and at minimum board eligible
Application method: Contact the Program Director (George Zhou, MD) by email
Licence requirement: Must be able to obtain a California medical license
Summary: Advanced training in adult liver transplant anesthesiology covering liver transplant recipients, living liver donors, major hepatic resection and complex open vascular surgery, with integration into Stanford's multidisciplinary transplant team (about 160 adult liver transplants per year).

title: Obstetric Anesthesiology and Maternal Health Research Advanced Clinical Experience
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine — Division of Obstetric Anesthesiology and Maternal Health
Eligibility: Applicants must have a strong commitment to research or other endeavours within Obstetric Anesthesiology and Maternal Health
Application method: Email CV and a brief letter of interest to Dr. Brendan Carvalho
Funding: Minimum two clinical days per week in the operating room; opportunity for extra clinical work for additional remuneration
Summary: A one-year (extendable to two-year) research-focused ACE in the Division of Obstetric Anesthesiology and Maternal Health, with mentored research and scholarship tailored to the trainee alongside a minimum of two operating-room days per week.

title: Advanced Clinical Experience in Pediatric Regional Anesthesia
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine — Pediatric Anesthesia
Deadline: Applications accepted through March 31 for August 1 start
Eligibility: Must be American Board of Anesthesiology certified or eligible to practice pediatric anesthesiology in the United States
Application method: Application form, CV, personal statement, 3 letters of recommendation, medical school diploma and residency completion documents sent to the Program Administrator
Funding: 50% Clinical Instructor (attending pediatric anesthesiologist) / 50% Clinical Scholar position
Summary: An advanced clinical experience in pediatric regional anesthesia combining a 50% attending pediatric anesthesiologist role with 50% scholar time focused on regional techniques in children and an academic project.

title: Regional Anesthesia Practice, Management, and Research Advanced Clinical Experience
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine — Division of Regional Anesthesia
Eligibility: Completed an ACGME-accredited (or equivalent) anesthesiology residency with a solid foundation in regional anesthesia
Application method: Completed application form, CV, three letters of recommendation, personal statement, medical school diploma and proof of medical licensure
Licence requirement: Proof of medical licensure required with application
Summary: An ACE for anesthesiologists seeking scholarship and management skills to build, direct and innovate regional anesthesia programmes, with an individualised curriculum in practice management, leadership, teaching and research.

title: T32 Research Fellowship — Research in Anesthesia Training Program (ReAP)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Duration: Two-year training experiences anticipated for most candidates
Eligibility: MD/PhD, MD, PhD or comparable doctoral degree; must be a US citizen, non-citizen national or lawful permanent resident
International applicants: Individuals on temporary or student visas are not eligible
Positions: Four trainees in total, two appointed per year
Visa support: Not eligible on temporary visas; post-residency fellowship programme does not sponsor H1B visas and J1 applicants are not eligible
Licence requirement: Post-residency clinical trainees must have a California Medical License before beginning
Summary: An NIH-funded T32 programme that trains future leaders in academic anesthesia through mentored research in neuroscience/pain, injury/inflammation/immunity, and outcomes research/bioinformatics.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Anesthesia Clinical Instructor Program
Department: Department of Anesthesia and Perioperative Care
Deadline: Rolling until a candidate has been selected
Eligibility: Completed anesthesiology training plus advanced fellowship training in pediatric anesthesiology or adult cardiac anesthesiology
International applicants: International applicants should have similar training in their respective countries
Application method: Send letter of interest, CV and three letters of recommendation to Dr. Anshuman Sharma by email
Funding: Appointed as clinical instructor with faculty-based benefits (including accrual of 2 vacation days per month)
Summary: A one-year clinical instructor year focused on perioperative anesthetic care of pediatric patients with complex congenital heart defects in cardiac operating rooms, catheterisation and electrophysiology labs, with academic days and a month in the pediatric cardiac ICU.

title: Trauma and Acute Care Surgery Anesthesia Clinical Instructor Program
Department: Department of Anesthesia and Perioperative Care (Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital)
Funding: Employed by UCSF; average of three days per week as an attending anesthesiologist; department-funded ECO 1 echo course, ATLS and conference attendance
Summary: A 12-month UCSF/ZSFG programme preparing anesthesiologists to lead in trauma and acute care anesthesia, combining attending work with supervised trauma call, research or QI projects, POCUS/echo training and teaching.

title: Perioperative Quality and Patient Safety Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia and Perioperative Care
Deadline: Rolling until a candidate has been accepted
Eligibility: Graduate of an ACGME anesthesia residency; must be board eligible or certified
Application method: Email CV, 1-page description of interests/goals and 3 letters of recommendation to Dr. Linda Liu
Funding: Clinical instructor work 2 days/week with 50% call commitment in the general ORs provides salary support
Summary: A tailored fellowship in perioperative quality improvement and patient safety in which the fellow helps lead departmental QI meetings and M&M conferences and leads department-wide quality initiatives.

title: Perioperative Informatics Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology & Perioperative Medicine — Division of Perioperative Medicine (Bioinformatics)
Eligibility: At least basic familiarity with relational databases and computer programming, including a working knowledge of SQL and ideally at least one other software language
Summary: A one-year non-ACGME accredited fellowship in perioperative informatics offered by UCLA's Department of Anesthesiology & Perioperative Medicine.

title: Pediatric Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology & Pain Medicine (Seattle Children's Hospital)
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-, RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited residency; open to fellowship-trained pediatric anesthesiologists, pediatricians, pediatric neurologists, family practice physicians and child psychiatrists
International applicants: Foreign national physicians who meet eligibility requirements are accepted (J-1 via ECFMG)
Application method: ERAS; NRMP December match cycle (Pain Medicine – Pediatric, 1918530F2)
Funding: Stipend per UW GME schedule; academic allowance subject to available funding
Visa support: J-1 (ECFMG) accepted; H-1B generally not sponsored unless the fellow is otherwise ineligible for J-1
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a Washington State provider license
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited pediatric pain medicine fellowship based in the interdisciplinary pain team at Seattle Children's Hospital, covering acute, recurrent, chronic and cancer pain in infants, children and adolescents and leading to pain medicine sub-board eligibility.

title: Global Health Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology with the Hubert-Yeargan Center for Global Health
Deadline: Applications accepted each fall for the following July start
Eligibility: Internal and external candidates are encouraged to apply during their PGY3/4 year
Application method: Contact Dr. Nathan Thielman by email
Summary: The Anesthesia Global Health Fellowship offers physicians in post-graduate training the opportunity to address health disparities in resource-poor settings and acquire clinical and research skills relevant to careers in global health, with tracks tailored to each fellow.

title: Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology (ACTA) Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, University of Michigan Medical School
Duration: One year (12 months of clinical rotations)
Eligibility: Satisfactory or anticipated completion of an ACGME anesthesiology residency in the U.S.; certification or anticipated eligibility for the American Board of Anesthesiology exam
Funding: Salary commensurate with a House Officer at an equivalent level of training (HOA contract)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing advanced training in the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care of adults undergoing cardiac, thoracic and intrathoracic vascular surgery, with comprehensive advanced perioperative TEE training at the Frankel Cardiovascular Center.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, University of Michigan Medical School (C.S. Mott Children's Hospital)
Application method: SF Match Central Application Service; virtual interviews March–May
Positions: Eight positions yearly (fellowship page; the fellowships index lists nine)
Funding: Salary commensurate with a House Officer at an equivalent level of training (HOA contract)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship at C.S. Mott Children's Hospital offering experience in complex congenital heart disease, neonates and premature neonates, fetal surgery and transplant, plus an awake infant spinal anesthesia programme.

title: Orthopedic Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology — Division of Orthopedic Anesthesia
Accreditation: Non-ACGME approved; fellow holds a clinical appointment as faculty lecturer
Application method: Complete and return the department application form; selected candidates interview with the chair, programme director and division members
Funding: Faculty lecturer appointment with 30% faculty time (including general call pool)
Summary: A fellowship giving in-depth training across the full scope of orthopedic surgery (total joints, trauma, sports, oncology and spine), including regional anesthesia, perioperative pathways, value analysis and operating-room improvement projects.

title: Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Anesthesiology Institute — Department of Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology
Start: August 1 (July 1 if required by military service or for J-1 visa holders)
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-, RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited anesthesiology residency; USMLE Steps 1, 2 and 3; ECFMG certificate if applicable
International applicants: ECFMG certificate required if applicable; J-1 visa holders referenced
Visa support: J-1 referenced (start date accommodation); other visa types not stated
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a temporary unrestrictive Ohio medical license
Summary: Established in 1976, Cleveland Clinic's ACGME-accredited adult cardiothoracic anesthesiology fellowship is the largest in the U.S., offering a high volume of complex, high-acuity cardiac, thoracic and vascular cases.

title: Cardiothoracic Critical Care Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Anesthesiology Institute — Department of Intensive Care and Resuscitation
Eligibility: Minimum five years of postgraduate training and completion of a fellowship in Critical Care Medicine, Critical Care Anesthesiology, Critical Care Anesthesiology/Emergency Medicine, Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology, Cardiovascular Disease or Pulmonary Diseases/Critical Care
Application method: Email completed application materials to CTICfellowship@ccf.org
Positions: Up to ten clinical fellows per year
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a temporary unrestrictive Ohio medical license
Summary: A newly developed advanced fellowship in Cleveland Clinic's 95-bed CVICU providing training in cardiac, vascular and thoracic critical care, mechanical circulatory support and heart and lung transplant critical care.

title: Pediatric Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Pediatric Anesthesiology (Children's Institute)
Start: Flexible; most begin July 1 or August 1
Summary: Established in 1999, this ACGME pediatric anesthesiology fellowship offers high-volume experience including congenital cardiac anesthesia, pediatric transplant, fetal surgery and pediatric pain across about 9,000 cases a year.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia)
Eligibility: Completed (or expected to complete) an ACGME-accredited residency in specialties including Anesthesiology, Neurology, Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation and Emergency Medicine
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited pain medicine fellowship at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia training fellows in evidence-based, multidisciplinary pain care.

title: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology — Division of Regional and Orthopedic Anesthesia
Summary: Trains physicians to lead and consult in regional anesthesiology, with ultrasound-guided nerve blocks and catheters, acute pain team management and high-volume ambulatory practice, plus chronic pain, pediatric regional and POCUS rotations.

title: Pediatric Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology — Division of Pediatric Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology (Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital)
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency AND a pediatric anesthesiology fellowship or adult cardiothoracic anesthesiology fellowship (the latter with at least one month of pediatric anesthesiology)
Application method: Email the Fellowship Director, Anthony Habib, MD
Summary: A fellowship to develop academic leaders in pediatric cardiothoracic anesthesiology through interdisciplinary perioperative care of children undergoing congenital cardiac surgery, catheterisation and electrophysiology procedures, with mentored scholarship.

title: NIH T32 Research Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology
Eligibility: Anesthesiologists who wish to become independent physician-scientists; U.S. citizenship or permanent visa status required
International applicants: T32 limited to U.S. citizens or permanent residents; similar non-NIH-funded research training is offered to qualified individuals
Application method: Review checklist, complete application form and send materials to Program Director Charles Emala, MD
Funding: NIH T32 funded; 80% research / 20% clinical effort
Summary: An NIH-funded T32 programme providing mentored laboratory or clinical research training (80% research effort) for anesthesiologists aiming to become independent physician-scientists.

title: Obstetric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology
Funding: Salary stipend at the Vanderbilt University School of Medicine PGY5 level plus health, life, disability insurance and retirement plans
Summary: Two ACGME-accredited one-year obstetric anesthesiology fellowship positions offering training in the comprehensive anesthetic management of pregnant women.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology
Application method: ERAS (ACGME Program ID 5304704001) with NRMP Match registration
Summary: Vanderbilt's multidisciplinary pain medicine fellowship combines extensive experience in advanced interventional techniques with rotations across multiple specialties.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt)
Eligibility: PGY-5 level following successful completion of an ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency
Application method: SF Match (Program ID 9888) with personal statement, diploma, letters, USMLE/COMLEX scores and ABA in-training exam report
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing comprehensive subspecialty education across all domains of pediatric anesthesiology, with an advanced pediatric cardiac anesthesiology fellowship available afterwards.

title: T32 Clinician Scientist Training in Perioperative Science Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology
Application method: Mail or email cover letter, specific aims, CV/NIH biosketch, mentor CV/biosketch and Other Support, and two recommendation letters to the programme director
Positions: Two to three new trainees per year (maximum 6 participants)
Summary: An NIGMS T32 programme preparing basic and physician scientists to optimise perioperative care through mentored research training with protected research time.

title: BWH Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesia Fellowship
inst: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Duration: 12 or 18 months depending on goals; combined ACTA/CCM two-year and 18–24-month research-combined options
Application method: SF Match with three letters of recommendation
Funding: PGY-5 starting salary $102,466 (2026) with health, dental and disability benefits
Visa support: Institution sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas
Summary: Established in 1992, the Brigham's ACGME-accredited adult cardiothoracic anesthesia fellowship provides comprehensive perioperative training in complex cardiothoracic and structural heart care across about 4,000 cases a year (an MGB Integrated ACTA fellowship is recruiting for 2028–2029).

title: BWH Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Application method: SF Match plus documents emailed to the programme coordinator
Funding: PGY-5 starting salary $102,466 (2026) with health, dental and disability benefits
Visa support: Institution sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas
Summary: A one-year critical care fellowship with a multidisciplinary faculty in which fellows spend at least nine months caring for ICU patients and supervising residents, with the mission of educating future leaders in critical care.

title: BWH Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
inst: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Application method: SF Match with three letters of recommendation
Funding: PGY-5 starting salary $102,466 (2026) with health, dental and disability benefits
Visa support: Institution sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas
Summary: Founded in 1985 and one of the oldest in the U.S., this 12-month ACGME fellowship offers more than 7,000 blocks a year at the main campus with formal didactics, conferences and research (an MGB Integrated regional fellowship is recruiting for 2028–2029).

title: BWH Perioperative Medicine and Ambulatory Anesthesia Fellowship
inst: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Application method: Department application form (PDF) and contact the Fellowship Director (David L. Hepner, MD)
Funding: Fellow works as an attending anesthesiologist 0.4 FTE; PGY-5 starting salary $102,466 (2026) quoted in FAQ
Visa support: Institution sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas
Summary: A 12-month fellowship developing the clinical, organisational and managerial skills of a perioperative medicine consultant through administrative rotations, didactics, projects and research alongside 0.4 FTE attending work.

title: Mass General Brigham Integrated Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia, Perioperative and Pain Medicine (BWH and MGH)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited integrated fellowship uniting Brigham and Women's Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital, with training across academic, community, VA Boston and Boston Children's sites in interventional, neuromodulation and minimally invasive pain therapies.

title: Cardiothoracic Anesthesia Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Completed an ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited anesthesiology residency (U.S. or Canada) before appointment
Application method: SF Match Central Application Service (match runs in June for the following July)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship integrating rigorous clinical care, research and a comprehensive didactic curriculum to prepare fellows for the most complex perioperative cardiothoracic challenges; sequential CT/critical care training is possible.

title: Critical Care Anesthesiology Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Physicians board certified, or in the process of obtaining board certification, in anesthesiology
Summary: Trains intensivists across dedicated surgical, cardiothoracic and neurosurgical ICUs at The Mount Sinai Hospital plus trauma at Elmhurst, with emphasis on advanced procedures, point-of-care ultrasound and echocardiography.

title: Liver Transplant Anesthesia Fellowship
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine (Recanati-Miller Transplantation Institute)
Deadline: Applications accepted every fall on a rolling basis
Application method: Fellowship application, CV, personal statement, USMLE scores, three letters of reference and latest in-service exam results sent to the fellowship coordinator
Funding: Competitive salary; includes part-time attending work and optional supplemental attending calls
Summary: A fellowship at one of the world's most active transplant programmes training fellows in anesthesia for hepatic transplantation and major hepatic resection, rapid infusion, cell salvage, veno-venous bypass and invasive monitoring.

title: Neuroanesthesia Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine — Division of Neuroanesthesia
Application method: Mail application form, CV, personal statement, USMLE scores, three references and latest in-service exam results to the fellowship coordinator
Summary: A 12-month neurosurgical anesthesia fellowship covering craniotomies, spine, interventional neuroradiology and functional neurosurgery, with a research experience, neuro ICU/neuromonitoring rotations and an international spinal-deformity mission.

title: Obstetric Anesthesia Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship managing more than 6,000 deliveries a year (30% high-risk), with NICU, maternal-fetal medicine and blood bank rotations and an antepartum anesthesia consult service.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship in acute and chronic pain management with hands-on fluoroscopy- and ultrasound-guided procedural training across inpatient and outpatient sites.

title: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Graduates of ACGME-, RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited residencies, or exceptionally qualified international graduates with ECFMG certification
International applicants: Exceptionally qualified international graduates with ECFMG certification may be approved
Application method: SF Match (applications from early January; virtual interviews March–May)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing advanced regional anesthesia training through extensive clinical work, teaching and research, including dedicated block-fellow supervision days.

title: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship at Mount Sinai West and Mount Sinai Morningside
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine (Mount Sinai West / Mount Sinai Morningside)
Eligibility: Current trainees or graduates of ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residencies in the U.S.; must be board-eligible
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (one of nine inaugural regional anesthesia programmes)
Application method: SF Match Central Application Service plus supplementary materials
Licence requirement: Must hold a New York State license or limited permit
Summary: A one-year programme across an orthopedic-centric hospital and a Level II trauma centre, training academic and clinical leaders in regional anesthesiology with trauma, truncal, POCUS and pediatric regional rotations.

title: Pain Management Fellowship at Mount Sinai Morningside and Mount Sinai West
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine (Mount Sinai West / Mount Sinai Morningside)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing interventional, multimodal and multidisciplinary training in acute and chronic pain across multiple clinical sites.

title: Obstetric Anesthesia Fellowship at Mount Sinai West
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (Mount Sinai West)
Application method: Contact the Fellowship Coordinator for application information
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited obstetric anesthesiology fellowship at a service with over 6,000 deliveries a year, covering healthy and high-risk parturients and non-obstetric surgery in pregnancy.

title: Cardiac Anesthesiology and Interventional Echocardiography Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine — Division of Cardiac Anesthesia
Deadline: Applications November 11 to March 1 (one year before matriculation)
Eligibility: Successful completion of an ACGME anesthesiology residency
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited cardiothoracic fellowship (about 1,200–1,400 cases a year) with extensive TEE, 3D and interventional echocardiography training for structural heart procedures, heart and lung transplantation, VAD and ECMO.

title: Adult Critical Care Fellowship (Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine — Adult Critical Care Medicine Division
Summary: The ACGME-accredited anesthesiology critical care fellowship of Johns Hopkins' Adult Critical Care Medicine Division, which staffs surgical, Weinberg and cardiac surgical ICUs at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Bayview Medical Center.

title: Liver Transplant Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Accreditation: Not stated (Advanced Specialty Training Program; fellows appointed as Assistant Professors or Instructors)
Funding: Faculty appointment (Assistant Professor or Instructor) with call obligations
Licence requirement: Fellows practise as independently licensed physicians
Summary: Trains academic leaders in liver transplantation and complex surgical patients through advanced perioperative management, TEE training and QI projects across about 100 liver transplants a year plus thoracic and vascular cases.

title: Neurosurgical Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine — Neuroanesthesia Division
Eligibility: Board-eligible in Anesthesiology with a history of clinical excellence and aptitude for research
Licence requirement: Must obtain a Maryland medical license
Summary: A one-year academic hybrid faculty-fellow track covering intracranial, neurovascular, major spine, functional neurosurgery and interventional neuroradiology, with protected research time, neuromonitoring and neurocritical care exposure.

title: Obstetric Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Funding: Annual salary approximately $87,546; educational fund and SOAP attendance allowance
Summary: Develops clinical experts in high-risk pregnancy management at a centre with about 2,500 mostly high-risk deliveries a year, including placenta accreta spectrum and fetal therapy cases, with required MFM and NICU rotations.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine — Division of Pain Medicine (with Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation)
Summary: A one-year multidisciplinary, interventional pain medicine fellowship run jointly with PM&R, with community and tertiary clinic experience and an optional partnership with the department's NIH T32 research programme.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine (Bloomberg Children's Center)
Duration: One year (two-year non-ACGME option with research or pediatric cardiac anesthesiology)
Eligibility: Completed 3 years of an ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency and board-eligible or board-certified
Summary: A one-year ACGME pediatric anesthesiology fellowship combining advanced clinical training, education and research, with a two-year non-ACGME option for independent research or pediatric cardiac anesthesiology.

title: Regional Anesthesiology & Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Deadline: Applications accepted through April 15 (SF Match registration opens in January)
Eligibility: ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency, or ECFMG-certified applicants from ACGME-I/RCPSC programmes or via the Exceptionally Qualified Applicant Pathway
International applicants: Accepted via ECFMG certification and the Exceptionally Qualified Applicant Pathway (GMEC approval required)
Application method: SF Match with at least 3 letters of recommendation; virtual interviews via Thalamus
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a Maryland medical license (or registration as an unregistered medical practitioner)
Summary: A one-year ACGME fellowship developing skills in basic to advanced regional nerve blocks and acute pain medicine across Johns Hopkins Hospital, Bayview and an ambulatory surgery centre.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine (Bloomberg Children's Center)
Summary: Trains pediatric intensivists to be exemplary, humanistic clinicians and future leaders in research, child advocacy, systems-based practice and medical education.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine
Duration: 1 year (two-year option combining core year with cardiac, regional or pain sub-specialty training)
Deadline: BCH preferred application deadline April 15, 2026; page states the programme is not accepting 2026-2027 or 2027-2028 applications
International applicants: Must pass USMLE Step 1 before applying; ECFMG certification in advance strongly preferred
Summary: Boston Children's core one-year ACGME pediatric anesthesiology fellowship, balancing clinical care with didactic instruction and research, which can be coupled with an advanced year in cardiac, regional or pain medicine.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Completed pediatric anesthesia fellowship or adult cardiothoracic anesthesia fellowship
Application method: Email standard application form, three letters, USMLE report, CA1/CA2 in-training exam scores, ECFMG certificate (if applicable), statement of interest and CV to anesfellowship@childrens.harvard.edu
Summary: An advanced ACGME-accredited fellowship of six months to one year in pediatric cardiac anesthesia, open to graduates of pediatric anesthesia or adult cardiothoracic fellowships and accepting 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 applications.

title: Pediatric Regional Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Completed pediatric anesthesia fellowship or adult regional anesthesia fellowship
Application method: Email standard application form, three letters, USMLE report, in-training exam scores, ECFMG certificate (if applicable), statement of interest and CV to anesfellowship@childrens.harvard.edu
Summary: An advanced non-ACGME fellowship of six months to one year in pediatric regional anesthesia for graduates of pediatric anesthesia or adult regional anesthesia fellowships.

title: Pediatric Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine
Eligibility: Completed residency in Anesthesia, Physiatry, Psychiatry or Neurology
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited pediatric pain medicine fellowship open to graduates of anesthesia, physiatry, psychiatry and neurology residencies (page states 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 applications are not being accepted).

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship Program
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Duration: 12 months; two 24-month tracks (Academic Pediatric Anesthesiology; Pediatric Cardiac Anesthesiology)
Start: Generally August 1 of the year following the match (variable start dates negotiable)
Positions: Up to 12 annually (including 2 each for the two 24-month tracks)
Funding: Two-year track commitments receive a substantial salary enhancement
Summary: An ACGME-accredited fellowship providing comprehensive clinical, simulation-integrated and scholarly training to become perioperative consultants and leaders in pediatric anesthesiology, with 12-month and 24-month academic or cardiac tracks.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Anesthesia Fellowship Program
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine — Division of Cardiac Anesthesiology
Duration: One year (12 months); two-year combined pediatric + cardiac positions available
Eligibility: Completed 1 year of an accredited pediatric anesthesia fellowship or adult cardiothoracic fellowship; board certified or board eligible (ABA)
International applicants: Exceptional international candidates will be considered
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship giving supervised experience across the full spectrum of congenital heart surgery, catheterisation, transplantation, ECMO and fetal/intrapartum cardiac procedures with a 15-member faculty.

title: Pediatric Regional Anesthesiology and Pain Management Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine
Application method: Email application directly to Dr. F. Wickham Kraemer
Summary: One of the fellowship programmes offered by CHOP's Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine, focused on pediatric regional anesthesiology and pain management.

title: Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Duration: One year (two-year combined CCM/ACTA track available)
Deadline: Applications accepted from January 1 to March 31 of the year before the start date
Summary: A one-year ACGME fellowship at the Pavilion and Penn Presbyterian with about 3,000 cardiac and 1,400 thoracic cases a year, a CT-SICU month and a summer echo boot camp, plus combined CCM and research (T32) tracks.

title: Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Summary: A one-year ACGME fellowship training independent intensivists in adult surgical critical care, with an optional cardiac and vascular critical care track (minimum six months in the HVICU) and a combined two-year CCM/cardiothoracic programme.

title: Neuroanesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Duration: Can be integrated into a two-year neuro-ICU fellowship
Summary: A neuroanesthesia fellowship with progressive teaching responsibility, protected research time (including an NIH training grant option) and neurocritical care exposure, which can be integrated into a two-year neuro-ICU fellowship.

title: Obstetrical Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine (Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania)
Duration: One year (two-year combined OB/cardiothoracic or OB/critical care tracks available)
Eligibility: From accredited anesthesia residencies with CA-3 year completed by fellowship start
Accreditation: Conducted in accordance with ACGME Program Requirements for Obstetric Anesthesiology
Funding: $2,000 per academic year for books, journals or approved CME expenses
Summary: Two one-year positions at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania (about 4,000 deliveries a year) cultivating experts in uncomplicated and high-risk perinatal care, with combined cardio-obstetrics and maternal critical care tracks.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Summary: A one-year pain medicine fellowship starting each July 1 with four positions, filled through ERAS and the NRMP pain match.

title: Perioperative Management, Quality and Safety Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Eligibility: Operating room experience mandatory; candidates from anesthesia (including CRNA), surgery, nursing and physician assistants welcome; physician candidates must have completed two years of training in an ACGME-approved programme
Summary: A fellowship for clinicians envisioning careers in administration and management of perioperative services, with a focus on perioperative management, quality and safety.

title: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency by the start of fellowship
Funding: Attending salary prorated to days worked as an instructor
Summary: A year-long fellowship across Penn Presbyterian (Level 1 trauma), HUP and an ambulatory centre performing about 5,400 blocks a year, with a dedicated acute pain service and part-time clinical instructorship.

title: NIH T32 Postdoctoral Research Training Program
Department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care, Perelman School of Medicine
Eligibility: Primarily physicians (MD, DO, MD PhD or equivalent) with research interest in anesthesiology, perioperative and pain medicine; exceptional PhD candidates considered; US citizenship or permanent residency required
International applicants: US citizenship or permanent residency required
Application method: Email the programme directors (Dr. Max Kelz or Dr. Roderic Eckenhoff); appointment approved by the T32 Executive Committee
Summary: An NIH T32 programme training anesthesiology/perioperative physician-scientists to become rigorous, independent investigators through mentored research in NIH-funded labs across Penn.

title: Pediatric Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited pediatric anesthesiology fellowship in some of the busiest pediatric ORs in the U.S., covering general, cardiac, fetal, transplant, trauma, neurosurgical and craniofacial cases, PICU/CICU and acute pain, with strong mentorship and coaching.

title: Advanced Pediatric Cardiac Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia — Division of Cardiac Anesthesia (Heart Institute)
Deadline: Rolling, prior to the start of the academic year
Eligibility: Board-eligible/certified in anesthesiology; must have completed a pediatric anesthesiology fellowship by the start (adult cardiac anesthesiology fellowship graduates also considered)
Application method: Email application form and supporting documents to the fellowship coordinator
Summary: An ACGME-accredited advanced fellowship with 10 months in cardiac ORs, catheterisation and EP labs and cardiac imaging, one month in the CICU and a congenital-heart elective, alongside clinical or basic science research.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia
Accreditation: Graduates eligible for ABA Pain Medicine certification
Summary: A one-year pain management fellowship combining pediatric and adult pain medicine training with emphasis on pediatric inpatient and outpatient chronic pain, leading to ABA Pain Medicine certification eligibility.

title: Advanced Fellowship in Quality Improvement and Safety
Department: Department of Anesthesia
Summary: A six-to-twelve-month programme of formal training in quality improvement science and safety (including the Anderson Center's Intermediate Improvement Science Series) with a mentored QI project for national presentation and publication; can be combined with a clinical fellowship.

title: Pediatric Neuroanesthesia Fellowship (Non-Standard Training)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology
Eligibility: Fully trained anesthesiologists from abroad with a strong interest in pediatric anesthesiology; approval by CCHMC GMEC Committee on Exceptionally Qualified Candidates
Accreditation: Not ACGME-accredited; ACGME-recognised Non-Standard Training (NST) programme
Application method: Contact the NST programme coordinator; virtual interview and one-week in-person visit
Visa support: NST participants usually receive J-1 visas sponsored by ECFMG
Summary: An NST fellowship providing advanced pediatric anesthesia training with special emphasis on neurosurgical procedures, designed to develop foreign-trained anesthesiologists into academically oriented pediatric neuroanesthesiologists.

title: Advanced Pediatric Anesthesia in Education Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesia (with University of Cincinnati College of Education)
Eligibility: Completed a core fellowship in Pediatric Anesthesiology
Funding: 30% clinical time as part-time attending; 70% toward Masters of Medical Education coursework
Summary: A 12-month GME-approved fellowship for pediatric anesthesiologists interested in medical education, combining Masters of Medical Education coursework with part-time attending work.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Baylor College of Medicine / Texas Children's Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Baylor College of Medicine (Texas Children's Hospital)
Duration: One year (combined two-year pediatric + pediatric cardiac option)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship at Texas Children's Hospital, which performs more than 58,000 anesthetics a year including nearly 1,000 cardiac surgeries and about 40 liver transplants, with rotations in cardiovascular, regional, pain and NORA.

title: Pediatric Cardiovascular Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Baylor College of Medicine / Texas Children's Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology — Division of Cardiac Anesthesiology (Texas Children's Heart Center)
Eligibility: Most fellows have completed an ACGME anesthesia residency and pediatric anesthesiology fellowship; adult cardiovascular fellowship graduates also trained
International applicants: Outstanding international candidates with equivalent pediatric and adult anesthesiology training considered
Application method: Rolling application to the programme; SF Match for combined two-year fellowship
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship (since 1998) at one of the largest heart centres in the world, with more than 1,000 cardiovascular operations and 1,600 catheterisations a year and nation-leading heart/lung transplant and VAD experience.

title: Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesia Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (Texas Heart Institute at Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center)
Application method: SF Match with three letters of recommendation
Summary: A year-long ACGME fellowship at the Texas Heart Institute/Baylor St. Luke's specialising in adult cardiac, thoracic, vascular and transplant anesthesia, with electives in cardiology, perfusion and congenital heart surgery at Texas Children's.

title: Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (Texas Heart Institute at Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center)
Summary: An anesthesiology critical care fellowship based at the Texas Heart Institute/Baylor St. Luke's, combining medical, surgical and neuro critical care with comprehensive cardiothoracic and aortic perioperative critical care training.

title: Obstetric Anesthesiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Anesthesiology (Ben Taub Hospital; Texas Children's Pavilion for Women)
Application method: SF Match (registration begins January; rank lists due June)
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship at Ben Taub Hospital training leaders in the care of healthy and high-risk parturients, including a one-month fetal surgery rotation at Texas Children's.

title: Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Funding: Stipend per WashU GME scale (e.g. PGY5 $84,439); discretionary fund for books and training expenses
Summary: A flexible ACGME fellowship developing expert-level skills in cardiac and thoracic surgical anesthesia, with protected TEE time toward NBE Advanced PTEeXAM certification and a CTICU rotation in a 27-bed unit.

title: Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Summary: A 12-month multidisciplinary programme with at least nine months in high-acuity ICUs and three months of electives, plus mentored research, QI projects and CCM board review.

title: Abdominal Organ Transplant Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Application method: Send completed fellowship application and supporting materials to the Fellowship Program Coordinator
Visa support: Unable to support any visa sponsorship at this time
Summary: A one-year non-ACGME fellowship at one of the top U.S. transplant centres providing comprehensive perioperative training for adult abdominal organ transplant recipients plus complex hepatobiliary, vascular and cardiothoracic surgery.

title: Neuroanesthesia Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Application method: Send completed fellowship application to the Fellowship Program Coordinator
Visa support: Accepts a variety of visas but cannot sponsor new H-1 visa applications at this time; applicants already on H-1B may be considered
Summary: A tailored neuroanesthesia fellowship across five neurosurgical ORs (two with intraoperative MRI) treating about 2,000 patients a year, with optional participation in a 20-bed neuro ICU.

title: Obstetric Anesthesia Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (continuously since 2016); SOAP Center of Excellence
Summary: An ACGME-accredited obstetric anesthesiology fellowship for two fellows at a SOAP Center of Excellence with over 3,600 deliveries a year and about two days a week of scholarly time.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited pain medicine fellowship at a tertiary referral and Level-1 trauma centre with ample interventional and multidisciplinary training, monthly cadaver labs and built-in non-clinical days.

title: Adult and Pediatric Pain Medicine Dual Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Duration: About 6 months pediatric and 6 months adult curriculum
Accreditation: Pediatric-focused track within the ACGME-accredited Anesthesiology Pain Medicine fellowship
Funding: Stipend per WashU GME scale (e.g. PGY5 $84,439)
Summary: A combined pain medicine fellowship training consultants to manage acute and chronic pain from neonates to the elderly through roughly six months each of pediatric and adult curricula.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Summary: A one-year fellowship at St. Louis Children's Hospital (about 20,000 anesthetics a year) rotating through general, acute pain and regional, cardiac, pediatric critical care and ambulatory anesthesia.

title: Regional Anesthesia and Acute Pain Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Application method: SF Match Central Application Service plus 3 letters of recommendation
Visa support: Accepts a variety of visas but cannot sponsor new H-1 visa applications at this time; applicants already on H-1B may be considered
Summary: A 12-month programme preparing future leaders to start and lead an acute pain service, with four clinical days a week of inpatient and outpatient regional anesthesia and acute pain service plus one academic day.

title: Trauma Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, WashU Medicine (Barnes-Jewish Hospital / St. Louis Children's Hospital)
Eligibility: Completed an anesthesiology residency (U.S. or abroad) and passed USMLE Steps
International applicants: Residency abroad accepted with USMLE passed
Application method: Send fellowship application and supporting materials to the Fellowship Program Coordinator
Visa support: Accepts a variety of visas but cannot sponsor new H-1 visa applications at this time; applicants already on H-1B may be considered
Summary: One of only a few U.S. trauma anesthesiology fellowships, with seven months on the Trauma Anesthesia Service plus ICU and elective rotations, averaging 16 shifts a month.

title: Cardiac Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Duration: Combined two-year ACCM + cardiac option available
Summary: A cardiac anesthesiology fellowship covering complex thoracic aortic, heart-failure and transplant, complex mitral and robotic cardiac surgery, with expected certification in advanced perioperative echocardiography and management of cardiac support devices.

title: Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Summary: A one-year fellowship rotating through surgical/trauma, cardiac surgery and medical ICUs with electives and research, with the option to combine with cardiac anesthesiology over two years.

title: Neuroanesthesia Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Summary: A one-year fellowship with rotations in neurosurgical ORs, neuro-interventional radiology, neuromonitoring and neuro-ICUs plus neuroscience research, with built-in attending time for non-neurologic cases.

title: Obstetric Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Application method: SF Match; application documents emailed to anesthesiafellowship@yale.edu
Summary: A one-year obstetric anesthesiology fellowship for one fellow, including monthly Severe Maternal Morbidity Review and Maternal High-risk Cardiac meetings.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Summary: An ACGME-accredited fellowship providing advanced knowledge, diagnostic and technical skills in pain medicine while fostering bench, clinical and quality/safety research to train future leaders in chronic pain management.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine (Yale New Haven Children's Hospital)
Duration: 12 months clinical (can be extended for additional research training)
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-approved programme at Yale New Haven Hospital preparing graduates to become leaders in pediatric anesthesiology, with an option to extend for research training.

title: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Eligibility: M.D. or equivalent; completed ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency in the U.S. or Canada; in process of ABA primary certification
Licence requirement: Connecticut State Medical License required before starting
Summary: A newly ACGME-accredited one-year fellowship training ultrasound, nerve-stimulation and landmark-guided single-shot and continuous peripheral nerve blocks and perioperative pain management across pediatric, adult, trauma and opioid-tolerant patients.

title: Thoracic Anesthesiology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
Department: Department of Anesthesiology, Yale School of Medicine
Application method: Email CV, personal statement and 2 recommendation letters to anesthesiafellowship@yale.edu
Funding: Includes one day weekly as an attending anesthesiologist in general ORs
Summary: A thoracic anesthesiology fellowship with three clinical days weekly in thoracic ORs, one attending day in general ORs, interventional pulmonology time and no overnight or weekend call commitment.
